name: i3 Paddle
description: An in-wall dimmer with on and off buttons and one LED.

steps.text: Connect the white wire to neutral, the black wire to line, the green wire to ground and the red wire to the load.

notes: To choose relay or dimmer mode, hold the On button (dimmer) or the Off button (relay) while the switch is power-cycled.

verification.note: The i3 Paddle/Dial (Insteon Developer Documentation, December 2023) and i3 Paddle/Dial (Insteon Developer Documentation, October 2025) give only the wire functions; they have no installation procedure.

steps.text: Press and hold the SET button to enter linking mode.

notes: Software can do the same by sending Enter Link Mode (cmd1 0x09) with the group number in cmd2.
Pressing and holding any button, including the SET button, broadcasts Button Held (Link Mode), which completes manual linking and identifies the device to controllers.

verification.note: No owner's manual or quick start guide was found; these steps are read from the i3 Paddle/Dial (Insteon Developer Documentation, December 2023) and i3 Paddle/Dial (Insteon Developer Documentation, October 2025), which describe the SET button only briefly.

steps.text: Have the Hub start ALL-Linking as the controller, for group 0.
Press and hold the SET button to enter linking mode.
Wait for the Hub to report the new link.
steps.expect: The Hub reports ALL-Linking Completed with the device's Insteon ID

steps.text: Have the Hub send ID Request.
steps.expect: The device answers with its category, subcategory and firmware version

steps.text: Have the Hub send Enter Linking Mode (cmd1 0x09) with cmd2 0x01, for group 1: as an extended message if Get Insteon Engine Version (cmd1 0x0D) says the device is i2CS, and as a standard message otherwise.
Have the Hub start ALL-Linking as the responder.
steps.expect: The Hub reports ALL-Linking Completed with the device's Insteon ID

steps.text: Have the Hub send Ping to confirm the link.

verification.note: Assembled from this profile's linking steps and the standard Insteon commands Start ALL-Linking, ID Request, Enter Linking Mode and Ping; no document describes adding this product to a Hub.

The Insteon Developer's Guide (2009) lists Enter Linking Mode (cmd1 0x09, cmd2 the group) as required of every device but i1 ones, and the Insteon Firmware Update i2CS Developer Notes give it to an i2CS device as an extended message with a checksum, from a sender that isn't in its ALL-Link database too. This profile's engine entries make every version of the product i2CS; no document names this product.
Read from the From a Hub alternative to this profile's linking, whose steps are assembled from its own linking steps and standard Insteon commands; no document describes adding this product to a Hub.

steps.text: Press and hold the SET button.
Press and hold the SET button again to enter unlinking mode.

notes: Software can do the same by sending Enter Unlink Mode (cmd1 0x0A) with the group number in cmd2.

verification.note: No owner's manual or quick start guide was found; these steps are read from the i3 Paddle/Dial (Insteon Developer Documentation, December 2023) and i3 Paddle/Dial (Insteon Developer Documentation, October 2025), which describe the SET button only briefly.

steps.text: Turn off power to the switch.
Turn power back on.
Long-press the SET button after power is restored.

notes: Software can do the same by sending the Factory Reset extended command, which works only if its data carries the device's category and subcategory.

The i3 Paddle/Dial (Insteon Developer Documentation, December 2023) and i3 Paddle/Dial (Insteon Developer Documentation, October 2025) say a factory reset returns the switch's properties to their defaults; they don't say whether links are erased.

verification.note: The i3 Paddle/Dial (Insteon Developer Documentation, December 2023) and i3 Paddle/Dial (Insteon Developer Documentation, October 2025) say only that a factory reset is the same as long-pressing the SET button after a power cycle; they give no durations or confirmation.

steps.text: Remove the device from every scene, as a controller and as a responder.

verification.note: Read from how Insteon links work: a device left in a scene keeps links to it in other devices' ALL-Link databases. No document describes removing this product.

steps.text: Remove the device from its scenes first, so no other device keeps links to it.
Have the Hub send Enter Unlinking Mode (cmd1 0x0A) with cmd2 0x01, for group 1, as an extended message if the device is i2CS.
Have the Hub start ALL-Linking with link code 0xFF (delete), so the device deletes its group 1 link to the Hub.
steps.expect: The device deletes its group 1 link to the Hub, and the Hub reports the device's Insteon ID

steps.text: Have the Hub start unlinking for group 0 (Start ALL-Linking with link code 0xFF).
Have the Hub send Enter Linking Mode (cmd1 0x09) with cmd2 0x01, for group 1, as an extended message if the device is i2CS.
Wait for the Hub to report that the link is gone.
steps.expect: The Hub reports the device's Insteon ID

notes: Inferred: seen on three i2CS devices (Outdoor On/Off Plug 2634-222 firmware 0x42, On/Off Plug 2635-222 firmware 0x48, I/O Module 2450 firmware 0x41) linked to a Hub 2245, these steps should remove every link between the Hub and the device with no SET button press. First the device's group 1 link: Enter Unlinking Mode (cmd1 0x0A) is sent to the device while the modem joins as responder. Then the modem's group 0 link: the modem starts ALL-Linking with link code 0xFF while the device is sent Enter Linking Mode (cmd1 0x09).

Inferred: seen on an i2CS device (I/O Module 2450 firmware 0x41) linked to a Hub 2245: unlinking by the modem's own records left the device's records for the Hub's other groups, and an i2CS device answers a device that's in its ALL-Link database. So a device that still answers the Hub after removal may hold other records for it; a factory reset, as this profile's reset steps give it, should clear them.

verification.note: Assembled from the standard Insteon commands Enter Unlinking Mode, Start ALL-Linking and Enter Linking Mode; no document describes removing this product from a Hub.

notes: It replies 0x02 to Get Insteon Engine Version (cmd1 0x0D), as i2CS devices do, and broadcasts Button Held (cmd1 0x01), with its hardware version in cmd2, when any button is held, even with programming locked.
sources: Insteon Firmware Update i2CS Developer Notes
